evals.prompt: I need to add a 'save for later' feature to the checkout flow. I know we have a checkout controller somewhere but I don't know what calls what or which files I'd actually be touching.
evals.expected_output: Claude traces the checkout journey end-to-end with file + line references, then asks the engineer one question at a time to locate where the change lands.
assertions: Claude traces the journey with at least 3 hops, each naming a specific file and line number or method
Claude asks the engineer to point to where the change starts — as a single question, not a list
Claude does not ask all three Step 3 questions in one turn
Claude reads the codebase itself rather than asking the engineer to trace the flow

evals.prompt: We get a webhook from Stripe when a payment completes. I need to trigger an email notification when that happens. Where does the webhook land and what would I need to touch?
evals.expected_output: Claude traces the webhook journey end-to-end with file + line references from the entry point through to where a notification would be triggered, then walks the engineer through locating the change one question at a time.
assertions: Claude produces a hop-by-hop trace starting from the webhook entry point (controller/route/handler)
Claude identifies the file and method where the notification logic would be added
Claude asks one focused question after the trace — not a bulleted list of questions
Claude does not immediately tell the engineer what to implement before they have located the change themselves

evals.prompt: There's a nightly job that reconciles orders. I need to add a step that flags any order over $1000 for manual review. I've never touched the jobs layer before.
evals.expected_output: Claude traces the scheduled job journey end-to-end with file + line references, identifies where the flagging logic would live, then asks the engineer one question at a time about where the change lands and what it touches.
assertions: Claude traces the job execution flow with file + line references from the scheduler/entrypoint through to data access
Claude asks the engineer to identify which hop the change belongs to — as a single question
Claude surfaces at least one unknown or assumption in Step 4
Claude does not volunteer the implementation approach before the engineer has demonstrated they know where the change lives
